title: lazy loading attribute and dynamic insertion of src of a previously requested image outside the viewport
body:
This issue is for clarification about a difference of behaviors in between browsers, exhibited by this WPT test.
http://wpt.live/html/semantics/embedded-content/the-img-element/image-loading-lazy-available.html
https://wpt.fyi/results/html/semantics/embedded-content/the-img-element/image-loading-lazy-available.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned
added by @Emilio on May 28, 2021
https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/2481a913db/html/semantics/embedded-content/the-img-element/image-loading-lazy-available.html

The commit makes reference to step 6 of 

which in the current spec is 

> 6. If selected source is not null, then:


The test is basically an image already loaded in the viewport
and an image being constructed outside of the viewport with 

```
 let lazy = document.createElement("img");
   lazy.loading = "lazy";
   lazy.src = nonLazy.src;
   document.body.appendChild(lazy);
```

In Safari:
* The second image (lazy) is **not available**: `lazy.complete` is `false`, `lazy.width` is `0`
* scrolling to get the image in the viewport, create again an HTTP request, with a 200. 

In Firefox. 
* The second image (lazy) is available: `lazy.complete` is `true`, `lazy.width` is `256`
* the second image is already requested and taken from the cache **before scrolling** (as seen in devtools)
* Scrolling doesn't change anything as the image is already here.

In Chrome. 
* The second image (lazy) is available: `lazy.complete` is `true`, `lazy.width` is `256`
* Scrolling doesn't trigger any load in the network panel of devtools but the image is already here (without additional request)


I opened https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=248025
but I wanted to make sure the behavior of Firefox and/or chrome were mandated by the spec. Reading the current prose I'm not sure, even more so, when reading the section about lazy loading attribute.



https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/c7629f8760a93a5d13e8d104e83f79ecca916844/#the-img-element

> The loading attribute is a lazy loading attribute\. Its purpose is to indicate the policy for loading images that are outside the viewport\.
> 
> When the loading attribute's state is changed to the Eager state, the user agent must run these steps:​
> 
> Let resumptionSteps be the img element's lazy load resumption steps\.
> 
> If resumptionSteps is null, then return\.
> 
> Set the img's lazy load resumption steps to null\.
> 
> Invoke resumptionSteps\.
